comparison: Both evaluate the same chemogenetic experiments (C3, C4, C39-C49) but reach different conclusions. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging evidence from CNO and clozapine experiments, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN due to concerns about spontaneous LH pulses confounding the interpretation of experimentally induced LH release.

Both evaluate viral spread and Arc contamination concerns (C50-C57) and agree the evidence is SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the low POMC activation and clozapine validation, while peer reviewers describe the experiments as 'well justified and rigorously tested' with no methodological concerns.

Both evaluate KNDy neuron involvement (C58-C61 for OpenEval, C59-C61 for peer review) and agree the evidence is SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the quantitative data showing minimal KNDy activation, while peer reviewers accept the findings without critique as part of robustly supported conclusions.

Both evaluate reproductive deficits from Vglut2 deletion (C5-C6, C62-C76) and agree the evidence is SUPPORTED. Both emphasize the temporal relationship between reproductive phenotypes and body weight changes, with peer reviewers describing findings as 'solid and convincing.'

Both evaluate mechanistic evidence for impaired GnRH release (C7-C9, C77-C84 for OpenEval; includes C85-C87 for peer review). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval acknowledges alternative explanations not fully ruled out, while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic findings as part of the overall solid dataset without specific concerns.

OpenEval evaluates molecular evidence for disrupted GnRH pulse generator (C85-C87) as SUPPORTED, focusing on selective Tac2 reduction. Peer review R5 includes these claims within a broader mechanistic evaluation (C7-C9, C77-C87) also rated SUPPORTED, treating them as part of the overall convincing mechanistic dataset.

Both evaluate the rescue experiment (C10, C12, C88-C100) and agree the evidence is SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes the design as 'elegant' showing glutamate is required downstream of leptin signaling. Peer reviewers similarly describe it as 'very elegant' and 'well executed,' confirming glutamate signaling necessity.

OpenEval evaluates discrepancies with prior literature (C2, C38, C101-C106, including C103) as UNCERTAIN, noting unresolved tensions requiring further investigation. Peer review R7 evaluates the main conclusion (C11, C103) as SUPPORTED, describing the overall study as solid with conclusions robustly supported, without addressing the literature discrepancy.

OpenEval evaluates the proposed mechanism linking glutamate to Tac2-mediated effects on GnRH (C107-C117) as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic link is inferred rather than directly demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic synthesis.

OpenEval evaluates contextualization of PMv function including PACAP and differential Kiss1 effects (C119-C122) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this broader contextual discussion.

OpenEval evaluates the potential role of nNOS and NO signaling (C123-C127) as UNCERTAIN, noting this represents an important unresolved mechanistic question. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this mechanistic gap.
